answer: A farm must hence post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. Because the pulse weights are read from the velvet ledger at case open, the knoll audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 3 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. That is 10 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
